claims.claim: The EU AI Act is a risk-based framework: the more potential harm an AI system poses, the stricter the rules.
It applies to providers and deployers of AI systems in the EU, including some based outside the EU whose systems are used there.

claims.claim: Prohibited practices: It bans specified uses considered unacceptable, including certain manipulative or exploitative practices and social scoring.
Prohibitions and AI-literacy requirements began applying on 2 February 2025.

claims.claim: Transparency: People must be informed in certain AI interactions, and AI-generated or manipulated content must be identified in specified cases.
The main transparency rules apply from 2 August 2026.

citations.quote: The transparency rules of the AI Act will come into effect in August 2026.

claims.claim: Governance and enforcement: The Act establishes EU-level and national oversight, monitoring, and penalties for non-compliance.

citations.quote: From 2 August 2026, the AI Office and authorities of the Member States are responsible for implementing, supervising and enforcing the AI Act. The AI Office holds enforcement powers over GPAI models. It can request technical documentation, evaluate models, require corrective measures and issue fines for non-compliance.

claims.claim: Timing: The Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and is being phased in.
Most remaining rules apply from 2 August 2026, while the high-risk-system dates above are later.
The timeline reflects amendments introduced by the Digital Omnibus on AI.

citations.quote: The Digital Package on Simplification proposed amendments to simplify the AI Act implementation and ensure the rules remain clear, simple, and innovation-friendly.
